title: runtime/scheduler: sampled structured logging for dispatch decisions
author: Julian Moore
body: Context: During mixed-workload scheduler canary we’ve had multiple on-call investigations where metrics showed a short-queue p95 spike / queue depth growth, but we couldn’t answer “why did the scheduler pick this batch / why didn’t the short queue drain?” without attaching a profiler. This PR adds sampled structured logs for scheduler enqueue + dispatch decisions to make incident triage feasible from normal logs (with low overhead). Scope: runtime-only, no API changes. Summary of changes: (1) Adds a structured event emitter in scheduler hot path with a strict sampling guard (token-bucket) and optional always-on for debug builds. (2) Emits JSON logs with stable field names aligned to our observability conventions (see below). (3) Redacts/avoids user content: we only log counts/lengths and internal IDs (route/model, request_id hashed). (4) Adds a minimal unit test for schema stability + sampling behavior. Log schema (all fields present unless noted): event="scheduler.dispatch" | "scheduler.enqueue"; scheduler_policy="fifo"|"two_queue"; queue_class="short"|"long"|"unknown"; request_id_hash; model; route; streaming=true/false; prompt_tokens; max_output_tokens; predicted_prefill_ms (if available); observed_prefill_ms (if known); queue_depth_short/queue_depth_long; wait_ms; fairness_window_ms; decision="dequeue_short"|"dequeue_long"|"fairness_tick"|"backpressure_reject"; reason="short_ready"|"long_starvation_guard"|"capacity"|"admission_control"; batch_id; batch_size; kv_cache_bytes (optional); gpu_id (optional); build="runtime-1.19" (from existing build tag). Sampling: default 0.2 events/sec per scheduler instance (token-bucket with burst=2). The rate is configurable via config key runtime.scheduler.decision_logs.sample_rate and can be set to 0 to disable. We also respect RUNTIME_SCHEDULER_DECISION_LOGS=1 for temporary overrides in canary. Performance: A quick microbench indicates <0.5% scheduler CPU impact at default sampling. When disabled (rate=0), overhead is a single predictable branch. Operator notes: These logs are intended to be used in conjunction with the new wait-time histograms and queue depth gauges; they are not a replacement. Primary use is answering “was fairness guard firing?” and “are we rejecting long class due to admission control?” Example log line: {"ts":"2024-11-21T03:14:12.901Z","level":"INFO","event":"scheduler.dispatch","scheduler_policy":"two_queue","queue_class":"short","request_id_hash":"c8f1…","model":"llama-3.1-70b","route":"/v1/chat/completions","streaming":true,"prompt_tokens":214,"max_output_tokens":256,"queue_depth_short":7,"queue_depth_long":2,"wait_ms":43,"fairness_window_ms":250,"decision":"dequeue_short","reason":"short_ready","batch_id":"b-8842","batch_size":4} Related work: pairs with PRs adding queue metrics/tracing (PR #8444) and starvation guardrails (PR #8439).
commits: runtime/scheduler: add DecisionLogSampler (token bucket) + config plumbing
runtime/scheduler: emit structured logs on enqueue + dispatch with redaction
docs(runtime): add operator note for scheduler decision logs

conversation: Omar El-Sayed (review): Can we guarantee we never log raw prompts? Even accidentally via debug formatting? Also, can you include queue depths and the fairness guard reason so we can correlate with starvation alarms. Julian Moore (author): Yep—this logger never receives prompt text; it only takes token counts from RequestMetadata. I added a compile-time static_assert that the event builder doesn’t accept std::string payloads from request. Also added queue_depth_{short,long} and reason field. Marcus Reed (review): Please ensure sampling is per-scheduler instance and not global, otherwise we’ll miss events under multi-GPU. Also watch lock contention; avoid taking scheduler mutex just to log. Julian Moore (author): Sampling is per SchedulerContext; it uses atomic token bucket state and reads queue depths from already-available counters (no extra mutex acquisition). Logging happens after dispatch decision is computed to avoid affecting ordering. Sean Gallagher (review): Default rate seems low. For canary we may need more. Can you add an env override and document rollback steps if logs get noisy? Julian Moore (author): Added RUNTIME_SCHEDULER_DECISION_LOGS=1 (forces sample_rate=5 events/sec, burst=10) and documented in runtime/docs/operators/scheduler.md along with ‘set sample_rate=0’ disable path. Allison Grant (review): Field naming: prefer snake_case consistent with our logging_fields.h. Also request_id_hash should be explicit that it’s hashed. Julian Moore (author): Renamed fields to snake_case and added request_id_hash (sha256 truncated, salted with process-unique salt). Approvals: Omar approved after changes; Marcus approved; Sean approved with note to monitor ingestion volume during canary; Allison approved.
release_notes: Runtime: added sampled structured logs for scheduler enqueue/dispatch decisions (disabled by default unless sampling configured). Intended for on-call debugging during mixed-workload scheduler canary.
